set.descent_text: West Face tops out on Guye's south summit (where the route tops out and the register sits; GPS surveys suggest the north summit may be marginally higher) at ~5,169-5,172 ft alongside the middle and north summits, and the descent is a scramble/rappel traverse north along the connecting ridge rather than a reversal of the climbing line. From the south summit, follow the climber's path around the east (right) side of the middle summit to the notch beyond the middle summit. The drop into the gully here is loose, mossy class 3/4 slab; most parties rappel rather than downclimb it. The total rappelling on this route comes to roughly 100 ft, enough that many groups get by with an arm-wrap/hip rappel off a sling rather than a full rap setup, though bringing a rope and device is still the sane default. Important: there is a tree at the top of the gully between the south and middle summits that climbers should specifically NOT rappel from (flagged as unsound/inadvisable in route notes) — use the established sling/anchor lower or to the side instead. Past the middle-summit notch, descend the gully and slabs to the right (east side) to go around the north summit, then scramble up an easy gully to the notch on the north summit's north side. From there, a well-defined scrambler's trail leads down past a small pond, then west (left) back to the Alpental parking lot. Bring a single 30m+ rope and rap device even though the raps are short — anchor tat and rock quality are inconsistent year to year, and the loose gully rock is a real hazard for parties above/below each other. Expect 1 rappel as the norm on this route (occasionally a short second one depending on exact line through the middle/north notch), well short of full pitch length.
